mappings.note: Lists the stated conditions in which the sangatkaar joins in (gala baithna, prerna ka samapt hona) - narrative content of the poem. LO-7 rejected: no image or bhaav is being appraised, the options are facts the lines supply.

Gloss of 'taarsaptak' as the poem uses it. LO-2 rejected: that outcome is for the poem's own upaadaan (tuk, lay, yati, gati), and taarsaptak is a music term inside the content, not a formal feature of this kavita.
Who gives the main singer dhaandhas - straight identification from the poem. LO-7 rejected: nothing symbolic is asked, only who.
The motive behind the hichak (keeping the main singer's maan) is the poem's bhaav-paksh, the reading the poet builds his sympathy on. LO-6 rejected: no line states this, it has to be interpreted.
Reads the deliberate holding-back of the voice as insaaniyat - the poem's central emotional claim. LO-6 rejected: this is an appraisal of the bhaav, not recall of an event.
Poet's date and place of birth is biography. LO-6 rejected: it is not a kaavyabodh question on the prescribed poem, and the frame has no biography LO.
Manglesh Dabral's standing as a patrakaar is biography / literary background. LO-6 rejected: the poem itself is not in play.
Which title is NOT his - bibliography. LO-6 rejected: nothing in the set poem answers it.

Factual detail of the main singer's gaayan as the poem describes it. LO-7 rejected: the chattaan comparison is only quoted back, not asked to be interpreted - the item that asks its abhipraay is mapped LO-7.
Who sings alongside the main singer (bhai / shishya / rishtedaar) - content recall. LO-7 rejected: no bhaav-paksh is being weighed.
Why the sweet voice is weak and trembling is answered by the sangatkaar's sense of heenta - a manahsthiti reading. LO-6 rejected: the poem states the voice is so, but not this reason.
Names the alankaar (maanaveekaran) in a quoted line. LO-7 rejected: LO-5 is the only alankaar outcome in this frame, so every alankaar item goes there.
Why he accompanies, answered by the poem's stated purpose - strengthening the singing. LO-7 rejected: the answer is the surface purpose, not the pratik.
Whose voice is called sundar, kamzor and kaampti - identification. LO-7 rejected: the interpretive 'why is it called that' version of this item is the one mapped to LO-7.
What the sangatkaar conveys to the main singer - the poem's own content. LO-7 rejected: no kala-paksh or image is under discussion.
Who lifts the fading voice - factual recall. LO-7 rejected: only the agent is asked, not what the act signifies.
Who assures him he is not alone - identification from the poem. LO-7 rejected: nothing is being read as a pratik here.
The main singer's voice as the poem literally describes it (chattaan jaisi bhaari). LO-7 rejected: the companion item that asks what that upamaan MEANS is the LO-7 one.
The three relations the poet names for the sangatkaar - content recall. LO-7 rejected: the list is stated, not interpreted.
Whose voice blends with the main singer's - factual. LO-7 rejected: no bhaav or shilp question is posed.
Asks the abhipraay of the 'chattaan jaisa bhaari swar' upamaan - reading the image, so kaavya-saundarya. LO-6 rejected: the factual 'how is his voice' version of this line is mapped LO-6.
Since when (praacheenkaal se) - a fact the poem states. LO-7 rejected: no interpretation is asked of that antiquity.
'Sargam ko laanghna' is a figurative phrase and its taatparya is asked - explanation of the poem's kala-paksh. LO-6 rejected: it is not a dictionary gloss but the unpacking of a metaphor.
What he reminds the main singer of (his nausikhiya days) - content recall. LO-7 rejected: the reminder is stated in the poem, not inferred.
What he holds together (sthaayi) - factual. LO-7 rejected: no aesthetic judgement is invited.
The situation in which he holds the sthaayi (when the singer strays into anhad) - narrative condition. LO-7 rejected: the circumstance is stated in the lines.
What the sangatkaar has done since ancient times - content recall. LO-7 rejected: the item asks the action, not its meaning.
His bhoomika stated as the poem states it (holding the sthaayi). LO-7 rejected: the items that ask what that role SIGNIFIES for society are the LO-7 ones.
Whose mahattva the extract establishes - the poem's central message about the unsung accompanist. LO-6 rejected: this is the theme, not a detail recoverable from a single line.
By what means he conveys that the singer is not alone - the mechanism the poem states. LO-7 rejected: no image is being explicated.
Second wording of the hichak question - the reason is the poet's bhaav-paksh reading (preserving the main singer's maan). LO-6 rejected, as for its twin earlier in this file.

Why the main singer's voice weakens at taarsaptak - factual detail about the main singer, supplied by the lines. LO-7 rejected: the sympathy those lines create is a different question, mapped elsewhere.
Why the hichak should be counted as his manushyata - explicitly an interpretation of the poem's bhaav. LO-6 rejected: nothing in the text says this outright.
Who gives dhaandhas - identification (a reprint of the earlier dhaandhas item with a different option set). LO-7 rejected: only the agent is asked.
What the poet CONSIDERS the lowered voice to be (manushyata) - the poet's evaluative stance, i.e. bhaav-paksh. LO-6 rejected: it is the poet's judgement, not a narrated fact.
What singing at taarsaptak does to the singer - content of the lines. LO-7 rejected: the experience is described in the poem, not to be interpreted.
WHOSE voice carries the hichak - identification only. LO-7 rejected: the 'why the hichak' items are the interpretive ones and are mapped LO-7.
What runs against the sangatkaar's lakshya - a statement of his role taken from the poem. LO-7 rejected: the 'why does he hold back' items carry the bhaav reading, not this one.
Meaning of 'garaj' as used in the poem - a comprehension gloss. C-H1.2 rejected: no grammar operation is performed, the word is the poem's own.
Which kind of voice the sangatkaar reinforces (tootti-bikhartii) - stated content. LO-7 rejected: the phrase is quoted, not explicated.
Which phase of the main singer he recalls (the nausikhiya days) - content recall. LO-7 rejected: nothing is being read for its bhaav.
Abhipraay of the figurative 'sargam ko laanghna' - explanation of the poem's kala-paksh. LO-6 rejected: it unpacks a metaphor rather than reporting an event.
Names the alankaar in 'aawaaz se raakh jaisa kuchh girta hua'. LO-7 rejected: alankaar identification is LO-5's own job in this frame.
Names the alankaar (utpreksha) in 'jaise sametta ho ... peechhe chhoota hua saamaan'. LO-7 rejected: LO-5 is the only alankaar outcome available.
Where the main singer loses himself (anhad) - factual recall. LO-7 rejected: the item asks the place named, not what anhad evokes.
How the main singer's voice is (kadak, garajdaar) - description stated in the poem. LO-7 rejected: no interpretation of the image is sought.
Whose job it is to add a goonj to the garajdaar voice - identification. LO-7 rejected: only the agent is asked.
Who usually gives the main singer dheeraj - identification. LO-7 rejected: nothing symbolic is in question.
Name for sargam sung in a high register (taarsaptak) - a gloss of the poem's vocabulary. LO-2 rejected: it is a music term in the content, not an upaadaan of this kavita.
Who repeats the main singer's swar behind him - identification. LO-7 rejected: the act is stated, not interpreted.
Whose lakshya out-singing the main singer violates - identification of the sangatkaar. LO-7 rejected: the restraint's MEANING is asked by other items, which take LO-7.
Whose gaayan the sangatkaar makes effective - identification of the main singer. LO-7 rejected: the item that asks whose importance the poem establishes is the thematic one and is mapped LO-7.
Three-mark recall of what sangatkaars have done since ancient times. LO-7 rejected: the expected answer narrates the poem's content rather than appraising its bhaav.
Explains 'antara' on the basis of the poem - a vocabulary gloss of the song's parts. LO-2 rejected: antara belongs to the geet described inside the poem, not to this poem's own chhand or lay.
How the sangatkaar 'jaan padta hai' - the poem answers literally (chhota bhai, shishya, door ka rishtedaar). LO-7 rejected: the wording echoes the text, so this is comprehension, not an appraisal.
Turns on the poem being chhand-mukt and still holding the reader - a question about the kavita's form. LO-7 rejected: chhand and lay are LO-2's named upaadaan, while LO-7 covers bhaav and kala-paksh.
Attribution of the poem to its poet is literary knowledge. LO-6 rejected: the answer comes from the byline, not from reading the poem.
Literal definition of the title word - one who accompanies the main singer. LO-7 rejected: the items that ask what kind of PERSON the sangatkaar stands for are the pratik ones and take LO-7.
What the sangatkaar's work is - stated content. LO-7 rejected: the poem says this outright.
Gloss of 'antara' (the geet minus the sthaayi tek). C-H1.2 rejected: no grammar operation is performed, this is the poem's own vocabulary.
